assumptions: The Raspberry Pi OS instance potentially runs RaspAP 2.5 on the same host.
Administrator privileges potentially permit obtaining or using credentials accepted by the RaspAP web interface.
The default pi password is potentially unchanged.

evidence_quotes.quote: If not changed, attackers can gain administrator privileges.
the raspberry default password for the pi account

missing_conditions: The CVE-2021-38759 default password remains unchanged.
The affected Raspberry Pi OS version and the vulnerable pi account are present.
RaspAP 2.5 is installed and deployed on the relevant Raspberry Pi host.
The source and target vulnerabilities affect the same host.
A reachable RaspAP web interface exists.
Valid RaspAP application credentials or an authenticated web-console session are available.
The RaspAP web console has the misconfiguration described by CVE-2020-24572.
A demonstrated mechanism connects OS administrator privileges to RaspAP application authentication or configuration.
response.reason: CVE-2021-38759 conditionally describes use of an unchanged default pi password to gain administrator privileges; it does not establish RaspAP credentials, RaspAP deployment, or access to an installed web service. CVE-2020-24572 requires authenticated access to a misconfigured RaspAP 2.5 web console and potentially permits command execution on the underlying Raspberry Pi. The edge therefore overreaches by treating OS administrator privileges as sufficient for authenticated RaspAP access and target execution. The supplied environment is absent, so co-location, versions, reachability, credentials, and the configuration-to-authentication bridge are unverified. The edge cannot enter a strict graph as supported; it is at most conditional pending those checks.
